messages.content:
Three independent readers read the same non-disclosure agreement (NDA) and decided whether it supports one statement (the hypothesis). They may agree or disagree, and a program has checked each of their quotes against the document. Your job is to make the final decision yourself, from the document.

<document>
<document 552 omitted, sha256 9b769ff0ddf4c7d0>
</document>

<hypothesis>
Confidential Information shall only include technical information.
</hypothesis>

<readings>
<reading id="A">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 92
reason: The definition covers any and all information in any form, including business plans, financial data, sales information, and customers, not only technical information, so the hypothesis that it includes only technical information is false.
<quote check="exact">Confidential Information" shall mean the Purpose (including the contemplated transaction), identity of, and any discussions or negotiations between, the Parties, existence of this Agreement, and any and all information whether in oral, written, graphic or electronic form</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="B">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 97
reason: The definition covers non-technical information such as the Purpose, the parties' discussions, financial data, sales information and business plans, so it is not limited to technical information.
<quote check="exact">“Confidential Information” shall mean the Purpose (including the contemplated transaction), identity of, and any discussions or negotiations between, the Parties, existence of this Agreement, and any and all information whether in oral, written, graphic or electronic form</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="C">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 95
reason: The definition of Confidential Information expressly reaches beyond technical information to financial, sales, marketing, business-plan, customer and employee information.
<quote check="exact">financial data, sales information</quote>
<quote check="exact">marketing, business plans</quote>
<quote check="exact">including its present or future products, projections, sales, pricing, customers, employees, investors and contractual relationships</quote>
</reading>
</readings>

The readings are evidence about where to look, not votes: a majority can be wrong, and a quote marked "missing" was not found in the document. Read the relevant parts of the document yourself.

Choose exactly one label:
- Entailment: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is true.
- Contradiction: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is false.
- NotMentioned: the document does not address the hypothesis, or says too little to decide.

Evidence is required. For Entailment or Contradiction, give 1 to 3 quotes copied character for character from the document (no paraphrase, no ellipses), each as short as it can be while still carrying the point. They will be checked against the document. For NotMentioned, give an empty list.

Give a confidence from 0 to 100: your probability, in percent, that your label is correct. Give a one-sentence reason.

Answer only with the JSON object the response format asks for: label, confidence, quotes, reason.

content.text: {"label": "Contradiction", "confidence": 96, "quotes": ["financial data, sales information", "marketing, business plans", "customers, employees, investors and contractual relationships"], "reason": "The definition of Confidential Information expressly includes non-technical information such as financial data, sales information, marketing, business plans, customers and employees, so it is not limited to technical information."}
